# Your practice setup {#sec-practice-setup}

Every hands-on box in this book uses the same small dataset and the same
folder layout, so the commands work as written on any computer. This chapter
sets it up once. It takes about 10 minutes plus the reference build.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["1. Software<br/>conda env"] --> B["2. Practice reads<br/>4 samples, 500k pairs each<br/>(from ENA)"]
  B --> C["3. References<br/>GENCODE GTF + FASTA<br/>→ Salmon & HISAT2 indexes"]
  C --> D["4. Shortcuts<br/>$DATA, $REF, $WALK"]
  D --> E(["Ready for the<br/>hands-on boxes"])
```

## 1. Software

Install conda and create the `rnaseq-tools` environment, as in
[Where to run the analysis](computing.qmd#getting-the-software-conda). Then:

```bash
conda activate rnaseq-tools
```

## 2. The practice reads

The practice data are a slice of the **airway** dataset (GEO
[GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778)):
human airway smooth-muscle cells from two donors, untreated (`untrt`) or
treated with dexamethasone (`dex`), paired-end 2 × 63 bp. The script streams
only the first 500,000 read pairs of each run from ENA, about 25 MB per file:

```bash
export WALK=~/omics-walkthru-practice           # change if you want it elsewhere
mkdir -p $WALK && cd $WALK
git clone https://github.com/jpflores-13/omics-walkthru.git   # if you haven't already
bash omics-walkthru/practice-data/get_practice_data.sh practice_data
ls practice_data
```

```
N052611_dex_R1_001.fastq.gz    N052611_untrt_R1_001.fastq.gz   N61311_dex_R1_001.fastq.gz    N61311_untrt_R1_001.fastq.gz   RNAsamplesheet.txt
N052611_dex_R2_001.fastq.gz    N052611_untrt_R2_001.fastq.gz   N61311_dex_R2_001.fastq.gz    N61311_untrt_R2_001.fastq.gz
```

| Sample | Donor | Treatment | Source run |
|---|---|---|---|
| `N61311_untrt` | N61311 | untreated | SRR1039508 |
| `N61311_dex` | N61311 | dexamethasone | SRR1039509 |
| `N052611_untrt` | N052611 | untreated | SRR1039512 |
| `N052611_dex` | N052611 | dexamethasone | SRR1039513 |

(How to download public data properly, in full, is covered in the companion
guide [download-public-data](https://jpflores-13.github.io/download-public-data).)

## 3. The references

Salmon and HISAT2 need an **index** built from a reference
([formats](sequence-files.qmd)); `tximport` needs the matching **GTF**. All
three must come from the same release, here GENCODE v49 (human, GRCh38).
Choose a size:

| Mode | What | Needs | Use when |
|---|---|---|---|
| `chr22` | Chromosome 22 only | ~4 GB RAM, minutes | Laptops; learning the steps. Only ~2–3 % of reads map (they come from all chromosomes), **which is expected** |
| `full` | Whole genome, all transcripts | ~16 GB RAM, ~30 GB disk, 1–3 h | Real numbers; a workstation or cluster |

```bash
cd $WALK
bash omics-walkthru/practice-data/get_references.sh references chr22 4   # or: full
```

It downloads the GENCODE files, builds both indexes, and prints the paths.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Phanstiel lab members: skip the build

Prebuilt GENCODE v49 references are on Longleaf:

```bash
export SALMON_INDEX=/proj/phanstiel_lab/Reference/human/hg38/indices/salmon/
export HISAT2_INDEX=/proj/phanstiel_lab/Reference/human/hg38/indices/hisat2/hg38_gencode
export GTF=/proj/phanstiel_lab/Reference/human/hg38/annotations/gencode.v49.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf
```

Put these in `$WALK/env.sh` instead of the lines in step 4.
:::

## 4. Shortcuts for every hands-on box

The hands-on commands refer to the folders by **variables**, so they work
wherever you put things. Save them in a file and load it in each new terminal:

```bash
cat > $WALK/env.sh <<EOF
export WALK=$WALK
export DATA=$WALK/practice_data
export REF=$WALK/references
export SALMON_INDEX=\$REF/salmon_index_chr22        # _full if you built the full one
export HISAT2_INDEX=\$REF/hisat2_index_chr22/genome
export GTF=\$REF/chr22.gtf                            # gencode.v49.primary_assembly.annotation.gtf for full
EOF

source $WALK/env.sh          # run this (and `conda activate rnaseq-tools`) in every new terminal
echo $DATA; ls $DATA
```

`$DATA` means "the practice data folder", wherever that is on your computer.
The [shell chapter](shell-basics.qmd#variables-wildcards-and-loops) explains
variables.

## The folder layout

```
~/omics-walkthru-practice/          ($WALK)
├── omics-walkthru/                 the book's repository (scripts, conda files)
├── env.sh                          your shortcuts
├── practice_data/                  ($DATA)  8 FASTQ files + RNAsamplesheet.txt
├── references/                     ($REF)   GENCODE files + Salmon/HISAT2 indexes
└── work/                           where the hands-on outputs go (made as you go)
```

::: {.callout-note}
## About the macOS `zcat`

On some Macs `zcat file.gz` complains (it expects `.Z` files). Use
`gzip -dc file.gz` or `zcat < file.gz`, which work everywhere. This book uses
`zcat`; swap in `gzip -dc` if you hit that error.
:::
